• Efficient Use of Bandwidth
oModulation allows high -frequency signals to carry information efficiently, enabling multiple 
signals to coexist without interference. 
oExample: FM radio stations operate in different frequency bands (e.g., 88 -108 MHz). Modulating 
the signal onto different carr

ier frequencies prevents overlap.
• Signal Transmission over Long Distances
oHigh -frequency carrier waves used in modulation travel further with less energy loss compared 
to low -frequency baseband signals. 
oExample: AM radio waves use modulation to transmit voice signals over hundreds of kilometers 
because low -frequency audio signals cannot propagate efficiently.
•Minimizing Antenna Size
oFor efficient transmission and reception, the antenna size should be proportional to the 
wavelength of the signal. Modulating the signal to a higher frequency reduces the required 
antenna size.
oExample: A 1 kHz audio signal requires an antenna hundreds of kilometers long, but when 
modulated onto a 1 MHz carrier wave, a practical -sized antenna (~3 meters) suffices.
